32.history: The old ford below Dùn ìseal where the road west crosses its river. A careful household of the ford dug a grain pit under its byre floor against nothing it could name, and brought nothing of it to the sharing; in the lean storm season of the two thousand three hundred and seventy-seventh year the daughter of the house, Beasag, saw the division made by the count of mouths and the next spring told a neighbour the truth of the pit. Tormod Liath asked only whether she had told it of her own will, and sent to open the floor. The household was given until dark to take what it could carry and be off the ford's ground: the first punishment under the sharing that is remembered. It settled east of the vein and dug no pit under its new floor. The pit kept the man's name for generations, and stood empty. Eilidh Ghlas knelt here to her younger son's height when he went west to be fostered.
32.known_for: the hidden pit, and the first punishment

415.history: A settlement on a narrow hill in the near valleys, on poor ground. One of the four stone cups was ground here in Oighrig's keeping, and the copy was begun fastest of the three despite two false starts; the cups were sent back to the wheel when their levels would not match, until at the meeting of the cups the water stood level in all four. From that year its households measured their handful of coal by the one cup and its copies. An old woman of Cnoc chaol was the first to say at the slab, in the judgement of Gilleasbuig Beag, that the vein was never any one hearth's to keep behind a cloth.

502.history: A settlement of herders on the eastern plain, below the passes the panthers cross. In the two thousand four hundred and twenty-eighth year Iain of Muileann bhàn drove forty head of thin cattle into the passes out of season, against the custom of the crossing, and the panthers took thirty head in a night; he came down lamed at the hip. Twenty-seven years later he walked south to the warm springs on his stick, sat in the pool three days, and walked home whole. In the three thousand seven hundred and seventy-first year, when the rivers of the eastern plain ran low all summer, its households drove their cattle to the warm springs to drink, and the shared surplus held.
502.known_for: the cattle lost in the passes, and Iain's cure

411.history: An old field in the east whose wells fell a hand lower than any digger remembered in the two thousand and third year. A shepherd's boy walked three days to Dùn ìseal to say that the field banks his grandfather raised had cracked from dryness; the springs stopped outright, and the households walked off their old banks and cut new fields lower on the slope. Sìleas Bhàn refused to have the dead field pulled down, saying a bank tells a household what the ground once gave and what it stopped giving. The households came back in the three thousand one hundred and twenty-fifth year, cut new fields on the higher ground, and sank a deep well before they broke a furrow; the well did not fail again in the age.
411.known_for: the drought and the well dug first

387.history: A broad red-earthed rise near the eastern Seann Dunn, settled in the middle of the long years by households who called the ground around them empty though the Old Ones' middens lay a morning's walk away and plainly said otherwise. They dug into nothing of what lay there. The settlement grew into a place of some size by the three thousand three hundred and eleventh year, raising its houses of the red stone of the rise.
387.known_for: the empty ground beside the middens
